abstract: Historical essay by Soumitra Shukla and Alex Imas tracing reactions to technological change from 1750 to 2026, arguing that alongside job loss, the threat to an identity built around expertise has been a recurring concern. Closes with mathematicians' response to AI results in 2026.
keyFindings: Covers the spinning jenny, the Luddites, nineteenth-century craft debates, assembly lines, telephone and elevator operators, computers, automated sportswriting, AlphaGo and the 2023 Hollywood writers' strike.
In September 2026, 28 Fields medallists signed 'A Severe Misalignment of AI in Mathematics,' arguing that AI companies' goals and the mathematical community's are severely misaligned.
On October 6, 2026, OpenAI released over 700 manuscripts claiming mathematical results; Hugo Duminil-Copin told Le Monde 'They have annihilated my field of research.'
Concludes that work has carried meaning beyond income and that transitions will be painful but need not be bleak if people can still contribute and take pride in their work.
methodology: Narrative history drawing on primary and secondary sources (96 references).
qualifiers: No labor-market data or estimates. Imas is Director of AGI Economics at Google DeepMind.
